items.explanation: Systematic or market risk affects all assets and cannot be diversified away, so it is the risk that carries a reward in equilibrium. Firm-specific risk can be eliminated by holding many assets.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: As an investor adds more randomly chosen assets to a portfolio, toward what value does the portfolio variance tend?
options: The average variance of the assets
The variance of the highest-risk asset
The average covariance among the assets
Zero
items.explanation: In a large well-diversified portfolio the individual variance terms become negligible and total risk approaches the average covariance. That residual reflects systematic risk and cannot be diversified away.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: An investor diversifies across many countries. Which additional risk is introduced by investing in foreign markets?
options: A complete loss of diversification benefit
The elimination of all market risk
A guaranteed reduction in expected return
Currency or exchange-rate risk
items.explanation: Foreign investments expose the investor to exchange-rate movements that can add or subtract from returns measured in the home currency. Global diversification can still reduce risk but does not eliminate market risk.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: The risk-free rate is 3 percent, the market risk premium is 6 percent and a stock has a beta of 1.5. Which value is the stock's required return under the capital asset pricing model?
options: 12 percent
9 percent
15 percent
6 percent
items.explanation: The CAPM return is 3 percent plus 1.5 times 6 percent, which is 3 plus 9, giving 12 percent. Omitting the beta multiplier would incorrectly give 9 percent.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: In the capital asset pricing model, what does a beta of 1.0 indicate about a stock?
options: It is twice as volatile as the market
Its systematic risk equals that of the market portfolio
It has no systematic risk at all
Its total risk is zero
items.explanation: A beta of 1.0 means the asset moves in line with the market and carries average systematic risk. A beta of zero would mean no systematic risk, and a beta of two would mean twice the market sensitivity.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: On the security market line, what does the slope represent?
options: The beta of the market
The total standard deviation of the market
The market risk premium
The risk-free rate
items.explanation: The security market line plots required return against beta, and its slope is the market risk premium, the reward per unit of systematic risk. Its intercept is the risk-free rate.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: A stock plots above the security market line. Which interpretation is most consistent with the capital asset pricing model?
options: The stock offers less expected return than required and is overvalued
The stock has no systematic risk
The stock's beta is negative
The stock offers more expected return than required and is undervalued
items.explanation: A point above the security market line gives a higher expected return than the model requires for its beta, suggesting the stock is undervalued. A point below the line suggests overvaluation.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: A portfolio invests 70 percent in a stock with a beta of 1.4 and 30 percent in a stock with a beta of 0.6. Which value is the portfolio beta?
items.explanation: Portfolio beta is the weighted average of the asset betas, so 0.70 times 1.4 plus 0.30 times 0.6 equals 0.98 plus 0.18, or 1.16. Averaging without weights would incorrectly give 1.00.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: Which assumption underlies the capital asset pricing model?
options: All assets have identical betas
Investors hold the same efficient risky portfolio and lend or borrow at the risk-free rate
Investors pay no attention to expected returns
Short selling is impossible in every market
items.explanation: CAPM assumes homogeneous expectations, a single period, and frictionless borrowing and lending at the risk-free rate so all investors hold the market portfolio. These idealised assumptions are among the model's criticisms.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: Which set of portfolios makes up the efficient frontier?
options: All possible portfolios regardless of risk
Only portfolios containing a single asset
The portfolios offering the highest expected return for each level of risk
The portfolios with the lowest expected return for each level of risk
items.explanation: The efficient frontier consists of the portfolios that maximise expected return for a given level of risk. Portfolios below the frontier are inefficient because another combination offers more return for the same risk.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: Where does the global minimum-variance portfolio lie on the efficient frontier?
options: At the rightmost point, marking the highest-return portfolio
At the highest point on the vertical axis
It is not on the frontier at all
At the leftmost point, marking the lowest-risk portfolio
items.explanation: The minimum-variance portfolio is the leftmost point of the opportunity set and the efficient frontier begins there. Portfolios to the left would require negative risk, which is impossible.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: Which line represents the risk and return combinations available by combining the risk-free asset with the market portfolio?
options: The capital market line
The security market line
The efficient frontier of risky assets only
The characteristic line
items.explanation: The capital market line plots combinations of the risk-free asset and the market portfolio using total risk on the horizontal axis. The security market line instead uses beta and prices individual securities.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: An investor combines the risk-free asset with the market portfolio. What shape does the resulting set of achievable portfolios trace?
options: A horizontal line at the risk-free rate
A straight line from the risk-free rate through the market portfolio
A downward-sloping curve
A closed circle
items.explanation: Mixing a risk-free asset with a risky portfolio produces a straight line in risk-return space, because portfolio return and risk both change linearly with the weight. The line is the capital market line when the risky portfolio is the market.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Portfolio Management - Portfolio Risk and Return

items.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the CFA Institute Code of Ethics from the Standards of Professional Conduct?
options: The Standards apply only to candidates and not to members
The Code and the Standards cover unrelated subject areas
The Code states broad principles, while the Standards are specific enforceable rules
The Code is legally binding, while the Standards are only advisory
items.explanation: The Code of Ethics sets out high-level principles of conduct, and the Standards of Professional Conduct translate those principles into specific enforceable requirements. Both apply to members and candidates.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Code of Ethics and Standards

items.stem: Which subject area is covered by the Professionalism standard?
options: Only the duty to keep client information confidential
Only the fair treatment of clients
Only the presentation of investment performance
Knowledge of the law, independence and objectivity, misrepresentation and misconduct
items.explanation: Professionalism groups knowledge of the law, independence and objectivity, misrepresentation, and misconduct. Duties to clients and performance presentation are covered under other standards.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which two standards fall under the Integrity of Capital Markets category?
options: Material nonpublic information and market manipulation
Loyalty and additional compensation arrangements
Fair dealing and suitability
Performance presentation and confidentiality
items.explanation: Integrity of capital markets addresses the use of material nonpublic information and market manipulation. Loyalty and additional compensation fall under duties to employers.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which set of obligations is grouped under the Duties to Clients standard?
options: Market manipulation and material nonpublic information
Loyalty, prudence and care, fair dealing, suitability, performance presentation and confidentiality
Knowledge of the law and independence and objectivity
Additional compensation and responsibilities of supervisors
items.explanation: Duties to Clients covers loyalty and care, fair dealing, suitability, performance presentation and confidentiality. Supervisory responsibilities sit under duties to employers.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which obligations are included in the Duties to Employers standard?
options: Independence and objectivity
Market manipulation and confidentiality
Loyalty, additional compensation arrangements and responsibilities of supervisors
Fair dealing and suitability
items.explanation: Duties to Employers requires loyalty to the employer, disclosure of additional compensation arrangements, and proper supervision of subordinates. Suitability and fair dealing belong to duties to clients.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: An analyst describes a guaranteed return product while knowing the return is not guaranteed. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Suitability
Referral fees
Priority of transactions
Misrepresentation
items.explanation: Misrepresentation prohibits knowingly making false or misleading statements about services, products or performance. Claiming a guarantee that does not exist is a direct misrepresentation.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: An analyst is pressured by an investment banking colleague to write a favourable research report. Which standard is most directly implicated?
options: Independence and objectivity
Fair dealing
Performance presentation
Market manipulation
items.explanation: Independence and objectivity requires analysts to avoid allowing external pressure to compromise the integrity of their research. Investment banking pressure on research is a classic example.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A member is convicted of a crime involving fraud. Which standard addresses this conduct?
options: Loyalty
Misconduct
Suitability
Confidentiality
items.explanation: The Misconduct standard addresses dishonest, fraudulent or deceitful conduct and actions that harm the profession's reputation. Criminal fraud falls squarely within it.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Before recommending an investment, a manager must determine whether it fits the client's objectives and constraints. Which standard does this describe?
options: Market manipulation
Additional compensation
Suitability
Fair dealing
items.explanation: Suitability requires an adviser to understand the client's objectives, constraints and risk tolerance and to make recommendations consistent with them. Fair dealing concerns equitable treatment across clients.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A manager allocates a hot new issue to favoured clients before other clients who placed orders earlier. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Independence and objectivity
Market manipulation
Referral fees
Fair dealing
items.explanation: Fair dealing requires that all clients be treated equitably when taking investment action, so favours based on relationship rather than a documented allocation policy breach the standard.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A firm shows only its best-performing accounts in marketing material while omitting the others. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Performance presentation
Confidentiality
Additional compensation
Priority of transactions
items.explanation: Performance presentation requires that performance information be fair, accurate and complete. Presenting a cherry-picked subset misleads prospective clients about the firm's results.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which obligation does the Confidentiality standard place on a member?
options: Publish client holdings in marketing material
Keep client information confidential unless disclosure is required by law or the client permits it
Disclose all client information to anyone who requests it
Share client data with competitors for benchmarking
items.explanation: Confidentiality requires members to keep information about clients and former clients confidential, except where disclosure is legally required or the client authorises it. It does not permit casual disclosure.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: An employee plans to leave a firm and solicits the firm's clients using confidential client records before resigning. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Market manipulation
Performance presentation
Loyalty to the employer
Fair dealing
items.explanation: The Loyalty standard requires members to act in the employer's best interest and not to take confidential client information when preparing to leave. Soliciting with misappropriated records breaches that duty.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A portfolio manager is offered a bonus by a client for achieving a target return. Which action is required by the Additional Compensation standard?
options: Accept the bonus without informing anyone
Reject the bonus because clients may never offer incentives
Report the client to the regulator
Obtain written permission from the employer before accepting the bonus
items.explanation: Additional compensation that could create a conflict with the employer's interest requires written consent from all parties before acceptance. The standard does not ban such payments outright.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A supervisor learns that a subordinate is repeatedly violating securities rules but takes no action. Which standard is most directly implicated?
options: Responsibilities of supervisors
Suitability
Referral fees
Independence and objectivity
items.explanation: The Responsibilities of Supervisors standard requires members to make reasonable efforts to detect and prevent violations by those under their authority. Ignoring known violations breaches that duty.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A member pays another professional a fee for referring a client but does not disclose the arrangement to the client. Which standard applies?
options: Misconduct
Referral fees
Priority of transactions
Market manipulation
items.explanation: The Referral Fees standard requires disclosure to clients and the employer of any compensation paid or received for referrals so the client can judge any conflict of interest. Non-disclosure breaches the standard.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A trader places orders intended to create the false impression of active trading in a security. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Performance presentation
Loyalty
Market manipulation
Confidentiality
items.explanation: The Market Manipulation standard prohibits practices that distort prices or artificially inflate trading volume to mislead market participants. Wash trades and similar devices violate it.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A firm claims it complies with GIPS in its marketing but does not follow the required composite construction rules. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Fair dealing
Suitability
Referral fees
Misrepresentation
items.explanation: Claiming GIPS compliance without following its requirements misrepresents the firm's compliance to prospective clients. A firm may state compliance only when it fully satisfies GIPS provisions.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A manager directs a portion of client commissions to a broker in exchange for research used in managing those clients. What are these arrangements commonly called?
options: Soft dollar arrangements
Referral fees
Incentive fees
Front-running trades
items.explanation: Soft dollar arrangements use client brokerage commissions to obtain research and services, and the standard requires that the benefit accrue to the client whose commissions paid for it. They must be disclosed and properly directed.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which standard governs how members should conduct personal trading relative to client accounts?
options: Additional compensation
Priority of transactions
Suitability
Market manipulation
items.explanation: Priority of transactions requires that client and employer interests precede the member's personal transactions. Personal trading ahead of clients, sometimes called front running, breaches the standard.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: An analyst receives nonpublic information from a company insider and trades on it before the news is public. Which standard has most likely been violated?
options: Performance presentation
Confidentiality
Material nonpublic information
Fair dealing
items.explanation: The Material Nonpublic Information standard prohibits trading or causing others to trade on information that is both material and not public. Acting on insider information before disclosure breaches it.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which action best supports independence and objectivity when a member attends a company-sponsored research trip?
options: Accept the trip only if all expenses are paid by the company
Publish only research favourable to the hosting company
Share the itinerary with competitors
Ensure the arrangement does not compromise objective analysis of the company
items.explanation: Members must judge whether travel or gifts from a company could influence their objectivity and decline arrangements that would create a conflict. The guiding test is whether the member can remain objective.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A client gives an analyst an expensive personal gift after a successful year. Which consideration is most relevant under the Standards?
options: Whether the gift could impair the analyst's independence and objectivity
Only whether the gift is taxable
Whether the analyst's firm has a marketing budget
Whether the client is also an employer
items.explanation: Independence and objectivity may be compromised if a gift is large enough to influence judgement, and members should consider whether their firm or clients permit accepting it. Modest tokens are treated differently from gifts that could create obligations.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A member votes client proxies. Which standard provides guidance on this responsibility?
options: Misconduct
Loyalty, prudence and care
Market manipulation
Referral fees
items.explanation: Loyalty, prudence and care treats proxy voting as an asset of the client that should be exercised in the client's best interest. A member should vote proxies thoughtfully or disclose the policy for abstaining.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A member discovers the employer is violating securities regulations and reporting the matter to the regulator is permitted by local law. What does the Standards guidance suggest?
options: The member must always resign on the first suspicion
The member should help conceal the violation until audit
The member should attempt to stop the violation and may report it, with resignation a last resort
The member should ignore the violation to protect the employer
items.explanation: Loyalty to the employer is subordinate to the law. Members should first try to address the issue internally, and if that fails they may report to the proper authority, resigning only when necessary.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A firm wants to advertise its strong investment record. Which practice best complies with the performance presentation standard?
options: Show only the composite with the best record
Use gross returns without stating that they exclude fees
Change the composite definition each year to improve results
Present returns that are fair, accurate and complete, including any required disclosures
items.explanation: Performance information must be fair, accurate and complete, with relevant disclosures about fees and compositing. Cherry-picking or changing definitions to flatter results misleads investors.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: A member refers a client to a colleague at another firm in exchange for a share of the resulting fees from that firm. Under the Standards, what must the member do?
options: Disclose the arrangement to the employer and the client before the referral
Keep the arrangement private to protect confidentiality
Decline all such arrangements as prohibited
Report the colleague to the regulator
items.explanation: Compensation for referrals must be disclosed in writing to the employer and the client so they can evaluate the potential conflict. Nothing in the standards bans referral fees outright.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Guidance for Standards I to VII

items.stem: Which statement best describes the nature of the Global Investment Performance Standards?
options: They guarantee a minimum investment return
They are a voluntary ethical framework for calculating and presenting investment performance
They are mandatory securities laws in every country
They apply only to hedge funds and never to other firms
items.explanation: GIPS is a voluntary, globally recognised set of standards for calculating and presenting investment performance. A firm claims compliance only when it fully meets the standards, which require independent verification for that claim to be strongest.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Global Investment Performance Standards

items.stem: Under GIPS, what is a composite?
options: The total market value of all assets a firm manages across every strategy
A list of all employees authorised to trade
A group of portfolios managed according to the same investment mandate, objective or strategy
A single client account with the largest assets
items.explanation: A composite aggregates portfolios that share the same investment mandate, objective or strategy so that performance is presented for like portfolios. Including dissimilar portfolios in one composite would misrepresent results.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Global Investment Performance Standards

items.stem: Under GIPS, what is the purpose of verification by an independent third party?
options: It guarantees that future returns will meet a target
It replaces the need for a compliant composite definition
It is required before a firm may calculate any performance
It provides additional assurance that a firm's performance presentation and policies comply with GIPS
items.explanation: Verification is an independent review that adds confidence that a firm has followed GIPS policies, but it is not required and it does not guarantee results. A firm can claim compliance without verification, though verification strengthens confidence.
items.reference: CFA Institute Level I Curriculum - Ethical and Professional Standards - Global Investment Performance Standards
